newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100, DAX, Ibex forecasts raised at JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100, DAX, Ibex forecasts raised at JP Morgan.

text.p: Strategists at JP Morgan Securities in London raised their end-1997 forecast for the UK's FTSE 100 index and increased their weighting on the UK equity market to "neutral" from "underweight," a research note said on Monday.
The brokerage also raised its end-1997 forecast for Germany's DAX index to 3,100 from 2,900 and its forecast for Spain's Ibex to 4,750 from 4,500.

Strategists Gary Dugan and Caroline Meroz at the brokerage said there were signs European equity markets will be able to make good progress with worries beign set aside over rising U.S. interest rates and increasing evidence of economic recovery.

Raising their FTSE 100 forecast for the end of 1997 to 4,300 from 4,000 points, they said UK corporate profits should benefit from an end to recent inventory rundown and that consensus earnings forecasts look set to rise, dragging the market higher.
The JP Morgan strategists continue to rate the German equity market "overweight" because of encouraging growth prospects and because the restructuring theme is "set to run and run."

And in Spain they raised their weighting on the equity market to "overweight" from "neutral," arguing that the increased likelihood of European monetary union suggested a fundamental revaluation of higher-yielding European markets.
